messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE — streaming tail p99 spike detected in eu-west2, multiple streaming stalls and reconnects. p95 ~850ms -> 2.1s, p99 ~1.2s -> 4.8s. Error rate up on streaming route /v1/stream (5xx + customer reconnects). Paging oncall@redwood. Runbook: https://console.redwood/runbooks/streaming-tail

Arjun (oncall): Picking up the page, oncall here. Starting triage. Any immediate customer-facing mitigation suggestions?

Maya (SRE): I started digging — seeing egress NAT exhaustion and elevated conntrack on eu-west2 egress nodes. TCP retransmit and TLS handshake spikes around 1719754300. Packet drops on node egress counters. Also seeing a surge in long-lived streaming connections that hold ephemeral ports.

Priya (NetOps): Confirmed — VPC flow logs show increased SYN retries toward 13.48.22.0/24 (egress NAT fleet). SNAT table usage trending to 95% on a subset of nodes in eu-west2-a. DNS lookup latencies also spiking for some flows (100ms -> 600ms).

Diego (CS): Customer reports: two premium customers seeing repeated reconnects and partial responses in live streaming. CS escalation opened (TICK-4821). Sharing customer traces with redacted ids.

Arjun (oncall): OK mitigation plan: 1) scale egress NAT pool + add ephemeral port range where possible, 2) reroute a portion of traffic to eu-west2-b/c standby egress, 3) enable short-term metadata-based sticky routing to avoid hot nodes, 4) if needed, failover streaming proxy to backup region for affected customers. I'll coordinate.

Maya (SRE): Trying quick wins first. Increasing NAT daemon replica count and bumping conntrack max on nodes in eu-west2-a. Command I'm running now (watching output):
```bash
kubectl -n infra scale deploy nat-egress --replicas=6
# increase conntrack on affected hosts via salt/orchestration
salt 'eu-west2-a-*' sysctl.set kernel.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
```

Maya (SRE): Logs from a problematic proxy instance showing handshake stalls: 
```text
[1719754305] WARN tls_handshake: handshake timeout after 4500ms, client=10.2.1.45
[1719754310] ERROR streaming: write failed: broken pipe, conn_id=xyz
[1719754315] WARN nat_snat: no free ephemeral ports, table_usage=96%
```

Priya (NetOps): I'll shift 30% of egress weight to eu-west2-b via route table policy and bring up an extra standby NAT stack in b. Applying reroute now. (will post ASG/route diff)

deploy-bot: deploy start: infra/nat-egress v12 -> v13 by Maya. CI checks passed.

Arjun (oncall): After scaling + partial reroute, telemetry shows p99 improving from 4.8s -> ~1.6s in the last 2 mins but some streaming stalls persist. Keep scaling and observe for 10m. If stalls continue, prepare for targeted customer failovers.

Maya (SRE): Observed reduction in conntrack on previously hot nodes, ephemeral usage dropping to ~60% after scaling. Still seeing a small class of requests that time out during TLS handshake — likely retries causing bursts. I'm going to enable short-term TLS keepalive tuning on proxies.

Diego (CS): Customer update sent: "We are aware of streaming interruptions in EU region, mitigation underway, updates every 30m." Customer impact queue updated.

Priya (NetOps): Route change propagated. Traffic now balanced across eu-west2 a/b/c egress. No packet loss spikes on new path so far. DNS tail latencies dropping.

Arjun (oncall): Good. Next: schedule handoff notes for oncall next shift, capture timing and mitigation steps. Escalate to SRE lead if we see another p99 surge > 3s. For now mark incident Sev2.

Maya (SRE): Adding runbook notes + relevant graphs to the incident doc. I pushed a quick fix to increase ephemeral port range on the NAT daemon config (short-lived). Need postmortem to consider autoscaling thresholds and proactive SNAT pool growth for streaming-heavy workloads.

incident-bot: Severity updated to Sev2 by Arjun (oncall). Incident channel pinned: incidents/1719754321. Please update timeline with actions taken.

Diego (CS): Opening support tickets for the two affected customers and flagging for credits if SLA breached. Will attach logs + timeline once final.

Arjun (oncall): Handoff: Maya staying for 15m to ensure stability, then handing to next oncall (Nadia) at 1719755380. If anything regresses before then, page me. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Maya (SRE): Copy — staying. I'll write the short-term remediation play and follow-up items for postmortem.

Diego (CS): I'll update customers after stabilization.

incident-bot: Incident closed to active mitigation 1719754412 — monitoring state. Please add notes for postmortem and link to runbook changes.
